statements.statement: Pure imitation learning approaches for autonomous driving face significant limitations despite large datasets and high-capacity models.
Even with 30 million examples and mid-level input/output representations, models can get stuck or collide with parked vehicles on narrow streets despite viable passing options.
Closed-loop operation introduces error accumulation and distribution shift from training data, leading to unreliable performance.
Pure imitation learning is insufficient to replace modular off-road driving approaches.
These findings highlight the need for additional methods beyond pure imitation learning to achieve robust autonomous driving.

parsed.type_evidence: Claims 1, 4 (limitations of pure imitation learning in autonomous driving) and claim 5 (insufficiency compared to modular approaches) from two different papers.
